Synopsis:
Dialogue with Raphael in House of Hope, when players try to escape it after an alarm goes off

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_HouseOfHope_RaphaelAppearance.json: The party has just set off an alarm inside Raphael’s House of Hope and are trying to escape while house defenses and attendants likely converge. Raphael — the aloof, dangerous master of the house — appears in a swirl of smoke and fire, asserting that the estate and its contents are his and accusing the party of trespass and theft. His manner is politely menacing: he can be both transactional (in other flows he’s offered deals, for example about Orpheus) and deadly, so this confrontation can quickly turn violent. In some versions Voss is not present, making this a direct one‑on‑one showdown where the player’s plea to leave is a last attempt to de‑escalate and flee.
- LOW_HouseOfHope_HopeSpirit01.json: First dialogue with Hope's spirit that happens after players get to House of Hope.Hope is a captive within the House, and has been driven mad by years of psychological and physical torture. Raphael keeps her alive because she astonishes him - and the reason for that is that no matter what he does to her, she holds onto the last of her hope and optimism. That fascinates him.In this dialogue, Hope introduces players to the House of Hope. They have arrived here deliberately, knowing that they are not invited, and that it is likely dangerous.Hope appears to warn them of that danger, and to help them, and also introduces the deranged vibe of the area.Note: When Hope speaks in all-caps, she is showing the manic side of her personality. Louder, more intense, and almost like she's possessed by a different, more deranged version of herself.
- CAMP_MonitorIntro_CFM.json: A devil named Raphael appears to lightly taunt the player, then whisks them off to the House of Hope (FOR_MonitorDinner).
- LOW_HouseOfHope_Archivist_SpeakWithDead.json: You are in the House of Hope’s archive room confronting Raphael’s archivist, a subordinate who maintained Raphael’s collection and legal paperwork and who can point you toward where Raphael hides his “secrets.” The narrator describes the figure as a corpse and his replies are broken and labored, so the archivist appears incapacitated or recently dead as he speaks. In this exchange he hints that some items and information are stashed in the boudoir and can answer questions about artifacts (for example the Orphic Hammer). Off‑screen, Raphael is the powerful patron tied to these holdings (he’s been seen offering deals in related scenes) but is not present for this immediate interaction.
- LOW_DevilsFee_RitualCircle.json: Dialog to invoke the ritual to go to House of Hope from Lower City.RELEVANT NOTE: This dialog will only appear at the first time players go to house of hope. Later, this never will be triggered again.

context: The party has tripped an alarm inside Raphael’s House of Hope and is trying to flee as the estate’s defenses and attendants converge off‑screen. Raphael — the aloof, dangerous master who keeps the deranged captive Hope alive because she amuses him — appears in a swirl of smoke and fire and calmly asserts that the house and its contents are his, accusing the intruders of trespass and theft. His manner is politely menacing and can quickly shift between offering cold bargains and lethal violence. In some versions this is a straight one‑on‑one showdown (Voss is absent), so the player’s plea to leave is a last attempt to de‑escalate and escape.
